title: Make Your Own Game -- core lessons

meetings.planNotes:
New idea: setup() and draw() -- and your first object
Goals:
- Open Processing and run a sketch
- Explain that setup() runs once and draw() runs over and over
- Create a Blob from the SpriteGame library and put it on screen
- Use RGB numbers to pick any color you want

New idea: Writing your own class with extends Blob
Goals:
- Make a new tab and write your own sprite class using extends Blob
- Override drawSprite() so your character looks the way you want
- Use pos.x and pos.y to anchor every shape to your character's center
- Explain that extends means "built on top of something that already exists"

New idea: Velocity -- changing position over time
Goals:
- Use setVelocity(vx, vy) to give your character a speed and a direction
- Call move() every frame to animate it
- Explain what screen wrapping is and when it happens
- Use random() to make things different every time you run

New idea: Input -- the program reacting to you
The class splits: Mouse Group / Keys Group

New idea: Draw order -- the order of your lines decides what appears in front
Goals:
- Use Block to add ground, walls, and platforms to your scene
- Write a second sprite class, like Cloud, with the same extends Blob pattern as your character
- Explain draw order:  whatever you draw later appears in front
- Design a world with a theme that is yours

meetings.scopeAndSequence: Lesson 6: Collisions:  If This, Then That (day 1 of 2)
meetings.planNotes:
Today: touch the coin, score a point
New idea: if -- making something happen only when it is true.  Collisions give it something to be true about.
Goals:
- Use collidesWith() to find out whether your player is touching something
- Use an if statement so something happens only when it is true
- Keep score with a variable that changes, and show it on screen with text()
- Use a boolean to switch your game between two states:  playing and game over

meetings.scopeAndSequence: Lesson 6: Collisions:  If This, Then That (day 2 of 2)
meetings.planNotes:
Today: a game that can end
Continues from day 1.

Today: Build
New idea: Restarting -- and putting all seven lessons together
Goals:
- Combine everything you have learned into a complete, playable game with your character in it
- Add a restart so the game can be played again without closing it
- Make your own design decisions about difficulty, theme, rules, and how it ends
- Go through the real cycle:  build, test, adjust, test again

Today: Play-test and present
Continues from day 2.
